## Executive Summary

The TDEM inversion results show a chi-squared misfit of 1.025, indicating a good fit between the model and the observed data, as it is very close to the ideal value of 1.0, suggesting neither overfitting nor underfitting of the data. The conductivity range of 0.0002 to 0.0024 S/m indicates low electrical conductivity, which may suggest the presence of resistive materials such as dry or compacted soils, or potentially fresh bedrock at greater depths, indicating a geological setting that may include low-permeability layers. The reliability of the recovered model may vary with depth; while the upper layers are typically well-resolved, deeper layers may be less reliable due to the diminishing sensitivity of TDEM to deeper structures. Further analysis could include additional TDEM surveys with varied time windows or integrating other geophysical methods, such as seismic or electrical resistivity tomography, to enhance the understanding of the subsurface structure and improve the model's resolution.
